metrics.methodology: Latencies use 512 bounded geometric histogram buckets, starting at 1 microsecond and increasing by 5%; quantiles are nearest-rank bucket upper bounds. The last bucket covers the remaining duration range. All terminal client attempts, successful attempts, and failed attempts have separate histograms. Throughput is completed attempts divided by phase wall-clock seconds. Operations are attributed to the phase in which they start. Redirect counts include only terminal MOVED/ASK errors; redirects handled by the client are not observable here.

workload_stats.pacing_methodology: Offered requests are ideal period slots from workload Start until the dispatcher observes Stop or parent cancellation; the first slot occurs after one period. The period is one second divided by the configured aggregate rate, truncated to whole nanoseconds. A central dispatcher offers only the latest due slot over an unbuffered channel; missed slots, busy workers, stopped tokens, and tokens with no eligible operation are dropped, without catch-up requests. Started requests count actual workload SET/GET client calls; completed requests count their terminal metrics attempts. After Stop, offered = started + dropped and started = completed. Validation and service probes are excluded. These global counters are not attributed to phases.
workload_stats.guarantee: Only successful client SET acknowledgements are validated. Every write uses a unique immutable key. SET errors are ambiguous outcomes and may have executed; they are excluded from the acknowledged-write guarantee. Redis asynchronous replication can lose acknowledged writes during failover. This check establishes observed post-experiment readability and value equality, not a durability guarantee.

methodology: Fault is SIGKILL of the deterministic primary owning the lowest initial slot; the process remains stopped. Initial topology is three primaries and one synchronized replica each.

Time origin is the start of validated fault injection, including Docker ownership inspections before SIGKILL; successful command completion is also recorded. Redis event times are bounded by polling and request deadlines; views within a snapshot are concurrent and not an atomic Redis snapshot.

A sample collects direct CLUSTER INFO/NODES and replication/server INFO from all six managed nodes, then parallel SET/GET probes to all three initial shards. Poll interval is a delay after sample completion; actual timestamps define resolution.

Recovery requires five surviving nodes healthy with exactly one owner per 16384 slots, equal ownership maps, the original replica owning the failed primary slots, unaffected ownership preserved, and all-shard SET/GET probes succeeding for stable_for. Post-recovery probes continue to detect regressions.

Probes are separate from workload metrics and do not guarantee every request succeeded between samples. The workload success rate, latency distributions and error counts report client-visible operations, including terminal errors after cluster redirections.

Workload stops and waits for in-flight requests before verifying every acknowledged immutable write. Missing/corrupt reads during traffic also prevent a recovered outcome. Error-returning writes have unknown outcomes, not proven lost writes.

At most 1200 topology samples are retained (first 1199 and latest); dropped_samples records omitted intermediates. Milestones are retained independently. No process restart or redundancy restoration is attempted.
